findings.title: Queries get interpolated twice when shard splitting delegates to time splitting
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery()` (lines 49-52) now interpolates every target once via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` before grouping by shard. For each shard group, `splitQueriesByStreamShard()` then builds a `subRequest` from these already-interpolated targets (with the shard selector injected) and passes it to `runSplitQuery()` (line 163). But `runSplitQuery()` was changed in this same PR (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299) to itself call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on `request.targets` before doing any further work. As a result every outgoing sub-request produced via shard splitting is interpolated twice. This is confirmed by the updated test expectation in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single target that produces 4 shard groups: 1 initial call + 4 repeats, one per group). Re-running interpolation (including ad hoc filter application via `request.filters`) on a query that was already interpolated is unsafe unless that operation is perfectly idempotent: if the ad hoc filter insertion logic is additive (locates the stream selector and appends matchers) rather than replace-in-place, filters will be inserted twice into the LogQL selector for every sub-request, producing duplicated/malformed selectors whenever ad hoc filters are combined with shard splitting. Even when harmless, this duplicates work on every single sub-request, multiplying with both shard-group count and further time-based sub-splitting inside each group, adding needless overhead. The sharding path should not feed already-interpolated targets back through a second full interpolation pass (e.g. give `runSplitQuery` an option to skip interpolation when the caller has already applied it, or make interpolation happen exactly once at a single, well-defined entry point).

findings.title: No test exercises the double-interpolation risk with non-idempotent ad hoc filters
findings.body: The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' only asserts the call count of `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` (now 5 instead of 1), and the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test mocks `applyTemplateVariables`/`replace` with a plain, idempotent string `.replace()` that leaves no trace once a variable has been substituted. Neither test exercises a scenario where `request.filters` (ad hoc filters) are set and the interpolation/filter-insertion step is additive rather than idempotent. Since `applyTemplateVariables` is now invoked twice per sub-request when shard splitting delegates to `runSplitQuery` (once in `runShardSplitQuery`, once inside the delegated call), there is no coverage proving that ad hoc filters, or any other non-idempotent transformation performed by `applyTemplateVariables`, are not duplicated in the final query sent to the backend.
